method: Independent lens review of captured evidence. The director opened every screenshot for a surface before scoring it, read the axe and capture results, and scored without sight of any other director's scores.
overallNote: Scored purely on control affordance, hit targets and state legibility, from static captures only. The recurring defect across the suite is a vocabulary problem rather than a craft problem: the bordered pill means "static tag" on task cards, "tap-to-filter" on the mobile board, and "editable field" in the task detail; the hollow circle means "complete me" in Tasks, "future milestone" in Timeline and pure decoration on About; and equal-width bordered cells mean "inert reassurance" on Pricing while looking exactly like a segmented control. Where a single rule is applied the work is genuinely strong — the selected-note left bar in Notes, the arrow semantics on the landing CTAs, the complete/next/upcoming encoding on the Timeline axis, and the "press e / j or k" hint in the task modal, which is the best piece of interaction teaching in the product. The two things I would fix first suite-wide are (1) one consistent treatment for "this is editable", applied identically in the task detail field column, the list-view cells and the board cards, and (2) selected states that cannot be misread, starting with Timeline/Milestones where the fill currently appears to contradict the rendered view. Three surfaces also carry unsignalled clipping — the Priority column truncated at the desktop list edge, the nested horizontal scrolls on the mobile board, and the clipped active Notebook tab on mobile. No veto: nothing here would block a real user or embarrass the company, but nothing is at the 9.5 floor either. Ceiling caveat that applies to all seven scores: these are stills, so hover, focus-visible rings, keyboard traversal, drag feedback, pressed/disabled/loading states and real CSS target sizes are all invisible, and the clean axe run (zero violations across sixteen captures, all HTTP 200, no console errors) does not cover target size, focus order or dialog focus trapping. I have credited none of that unexercised behaviour.

surfaces.rationale: Board desktop gets the core grammar right: circular completion toggles on every card, filled green checks on the Done column, coloured status dots with a one-line explainer per column, and a 'Nothing held up' bordered placeholder in Waiting that doubles as a drop target. But the pill does double duty — 'Mara & Finn', 'Venue', 'Bar', 'Enquiry' are static tags drawn as bordered pills, and on mobile the column filters 'To do 3 / In progress 3 / Review 2 / Waiting 0' are bordered pills of near-identical treatment, so the same shape means both 'label' and 'tap me' on one screen. 'Filter', 'Sort' and 'Display' carry icon+label with no chevron and no border, so three popover triggers read as plain captions — Notes gets this right with 'Newest first ⌄' two clicks away. In list-desktop the Priority column is clipped at the viewport edge ('Hig', 'Lo', 'No', header cut to 'P') with no visible scrollbar or fade, so a field is unreadable with nothing telling you to scroll; each row also carries a square select checkbox and a completion circle ~30px apart with no separation. Mobile board nests two horizontal scroll regions (the chip row clipping 'Waiting', the In-progress column clipped mid-card) with no scroll indicator on either. The left rail's home glyph and the two bottom icons are unlabeled while Notes/Tasks/Timeline/More are labelled. The 'In development' toast sits over live table rows in both list captures. Static frames cannot show hover-revealed column menus (visible on mobile, absent on desktop), drag feedback on a board that clearly implies drag, focus rings or real target sizes; axe's clean run does not cover target-size or focus order, so I give none of that credit.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Split the pill vocabulary: give interactive chips (status filters, editable fields) a single consistent treatment with a chevron or hover border, and demote static tags to borderless text or a distinctly softer token — then fix the clipped Priority column so no field is unreadable without an unsignalled scroll.

surfaces.rationale: The modal's action hierarchy is correct and rare: one filled indigo 'Mark done' against secondary chips for status, assignee, date and priority, an 'OR Orla +' cluster where the + plainly means add-assignee, and a dashed 'Drop files here, or paste a link…' zone that unambiguously announces itself. The inline hint 'Press e to open a task full-screen, and j or k to move between tasks' with its own × is genuine interaction teaching and partly rescues the top-right cluster of five unlabeled glyph buttons (^, ⌄, expand, …, ×) packed at ~36px pitch. The field column is where it breaks: REPEATS ('Doesn't repeat'), CONTACT ('County Marquee Hire') and COPIES ('Make copies') are bordered chips, while TAGS ('Mara & Finn') and PROJECT ('The Orchard, events') are bare text and SOURCE ('From Notes · open source') is underlined — four affordance treatments for one class of field, so nothing tells you which are editable. The same status control that carries a chevron in list view ('To do ⌄') is a chevron-less pill here. The breadcrumb 'The Orchard, events / T-1' has no link affordance at rest. Beside 'DRAFT A REPLY' sits a small unlabeled ⏎ chip whose relationship to the button is unreadable. Mobile stacks well and 'Mark done' becomes a proper thumb target, but 'Reply or comment, @ to mention' wraps into two lines and crowds the draft button, and a stray rounded fragment sits above the sheet header. Focus order through the modal, escape handling and open/close motion are invisible here; axe's zero violations say nothing about focus trapping in a dialog it captured statically.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Adopt one rule for the field column — every editable property gets the same chip treatment and hover affordance, every read-only one gets plain text — so TAGS and PROJECT stop looking different from CONTACT and REPEATS for no reason.

surfaces.rationale: The selected-note state is the best in the app: an indigo left bar plus a tinted row on 'Saturday wedding, Mara & Finn.' leaves zero doubt about what the detail pane is showing. Search carries a '/' key chip, 'All notes ⌄' and 'Newest first ⌄' both carry chevrons, and the Type/Voice/Photo toggle marks Type with a tinted pill. Controls appear only where they apply — the two 'To review' rows expose triage buttons and the settled rows show none. The problems are in state and weight. 'Save note' is a light outlined button on desktop (secondary weight for the composer's primary action) and a grey-filled full-width button on mobile — two different treatments for one control, and with an empty composer there is no legible enabled/disabled state either way. The triage trio 'Keep / Turn into task / Delete' are three equal-weight outlined buttons of the same size, with the destructive one distinguished only by red label text and no separation from the constructive pair. The note body in the detail pane has no visible edit affordance at all — the primary object of the product offers nothing that says it can be changed. On mobile the active 'Notebook' tab's tinted background is clipped by the left viewport edge, and 'Private to you' collapses to a bare unlabeled padlock. Whether the body is click-to-edit, whether Delete confirms, and what the composer looks like once dirty are all things a static capture cannot show, so I score them as absent rather than assumed.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Give the note body an explicit edit affordance and give 'Save note' one primary treatment with a real disabled state, so the composer and the note both show plainly whether they can be acted on.

surfaces.rationale: The axis is the most sophisticated state encoding in the product: filled dots for complete, hollow for future, an indigo dot for 'Our next milestone', a taller 'Today' tick, and a bracketed cluster captioned '4 milestones' — complete, upcoming, next and collapsed all readable at a glance, with 'Live since 15 Jul 2026. Anyone holding the link can read it.' stating the sharing state in plain words. Against that, the primary view switch is ambiguous: 'Timeline | Milestones' shows the fill on Milestones while the page is plainly rendering the timeline, so the selected segment either contradicts the content or the capture caught a hover — from the evidence a user has to guess which view they are in, and that is exactly the failure my lens exists to catch. It repeats identically on mobile. Control affordance on the axis is essentially nil: the milestone dots are ~8-10px, the '4 milestones' bracket implies expansion with no chevron or button, and the callout labels ('We said yes', 'Menu tasting at The Orchard', 'Send the invitations') read as static captions, so a rich display offers no visible handles. On mobile the segmented pair sits flush against the standalone 'Preview' button at the same height and border weight, so four peer-looking buttons hide a two-plus-two grouping. 'Share' as a filled indigo primary and the 'Mara & Finn ⌄' project switcher are correct and clear. The hero — 'Mara & Finn', '79 days' — is correctly inert and mis-signals nothing. Hover states on the dots, whether they open anything, and touch behaviour on the axis cannot be judged from stills.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Make the Timeline/Milestones segmented control state unmistakable — selected segment filled and marked, unselected clearly recessed — and separate it from 'Preview' so the view switch is not read as a fourth action button.

surfaces.rationale: The clearest affordance work in the set. Exactly one primary — 'See the system at work' filled black — against one outlined secondary, 'Join the waitlist', and the arrows do real semantic work: the down arrow says in-page scroll, the right arrow says you are leaving here. Both are generous targets, ~48px on desktop and full-width on mobile. 'Products ⌄' carries a chevron so the one menu in the nav announces itself, and 'NOTES → TASKS → TIMELINE' in mono caps is honest static wayfinding that never pretends to be a control. Nothing inert on this page is dressed as interactive. Two gaps: the nav has no current-page state at all — 'Design', 'Pricing', 'About' sit in identical light grey here and on the pages they name — and the mobile header is a muddle, promoting 'Products ⌄' outside an unlabeled hamburger so one nav item lives at a different level than the rest with no visual explanation of the grouping. The subhead tints 'Notes, Tasks and Timeline' warmer than the surrounding sentence, which reads link-shaped for words that are not links here. Hover, focus-visible rings, and the behaviour of the Products menu are outside what these frames can show, so none of that is credited.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Add a current-page state to the nav and resolve the mobile header so 'Products' either lives inside the menu or the whole nav is exposed — one level, one rule.

surfaces.rationale: An editorial page with almost no controls, and it mostly earns credit the right way: the eyebrow 'A NOTE FROM THE FOUNDER', the headline, the body paragraph and the bold pull-line 'The mistake was assuming every project should work that way.' are all unmistakably inert — nothing here is dressed as a button, which is the harder half of my lens and it passes. The vertical indigo rule with a filled dot at the eyebrow is decoration that stays decoration. One collision: on mobile a hollow circle node sits on that rule beside 'A wedding may be the largest project someone ever manages.' — and a hollow circle is a completion toggle in Tasks and a future milestone in Timeline, so the same mark carries three meanings across the suite. The header inherits landing's two gaps: no current-page indicator on 'About' while you are on About, and the promoted 'Products ⌄' beside an unlabeled hamburger. Within the captured viewport there is no CTA of any kind, so a reader persuaded by the founder's note has nothing to act on until they scroll past what the evidence shows. Link colour and hover treatment inside the running copy, and anything below the fold, are not visible in these frames.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Retire the hollow-circle marker as decoration here — it is a completion toggle in Tasks and a milestone in Timeline — and reserve the shape for controls and state across the suite.

surfaces.rationale: The desktop reassurance strip is the sharpest static-looks-interactive failure in the seven surfaces: 'No charge / on the waitlist', 'VAT included / at the prevailing rate', 'Terms repeated / before purchase' sit full-bleed on a tinted band, divided into three equal cells by vertical hairlines, each with a bold label over a grey caption — that is the exact anatomy of a segmented control or a tab set, and it is inert copy. Mobile stacks it into hairline-divided rows and reads correctly as a list, which shows the desktop framing is the problem rather than the content. Above that, the whole first screen of a page whose job is to be acted on contains no interactive element but the nav — no plan card, no price, no CTA — while the subhead ('Compare the price, workspace limit and the terms settled today') promises a comparison that is entirely below the fold. That subhead also tints 'less while studying', 'Pro', 'limit' and 'Ethan' warmer than the surrounding text, giving link colouring to words that are not links. The nav shows no current-page state on the very page it names. The eyebrow 'PRICING' and the headline are correctly inert. Whether the plan cards below the fold carry proper selected states, hover, or focus treatment is not something these captures can tell me, and I have given it no credit.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Redraw the three-fact strip so it cannot be mistaken for a segmented control — drop the cell dividers and equal-width boxing for plain inline statements — and lift at least one real CTA into the first screen.
